questions.q: Which two engines run inside every SSIS package, regardless of whether it's still in development or deployed?
options: The runtime engine and the data flow engine
The Integration Services service and the SSISDB catalog
SQL Server Management Studio and Visual Studio
The SSIS service and SSDT
questions.explain: The runtime engine (control flow) and the data flow engine (rows) are the two engines active any time a package validates or runs, in development or production.

questions.q: Is the legacy Integration Services (SSIS) Windows service required to create, save, or run a package?
options: No — Microsoft states it is not required for those operations; it's for monitoring stored packages from SSMS
Yes — no package can execute unless this service is running
Yes, but only for packages built before 2016
It's required only for packages that use a Data Flow Task
questions.explain: Microsoft's own documentation states the Integration Services service is not required to create, save, or run packages — it exists to monitor and manage packages stored the legacy way.

options: A database, hosted inside a SQL Server Database Engine instance, that stores deployed projects, versions, parameters, and execution history
A standalone Windows service separate from SQL Server
A folder on disk where .dtsx files are copied for backup
A feature exclusive to SQL Server Management Studio with no relationship to SQL Server itself
questions.explain: SSISDB is a real database inside the SQL Server Database Engine — not a separate service — and it's the modern central point for deployed projects.

questions.q: What's the difference between design time and run time for an SSIS package?
options: Design time is building and test-running a package inside SSDT with no server involved; run time is a deployed project executing from the SSISDB catalog in production
Design time and run time are two names for the same thing
Design time only happens on a server; run time only happens inside Visual Studio
Run time refers only to writing T-SQL inside an Execute SQL Task
questions.explain: Design time is entirely local, inside SSDT; run time is production execution of a deployed project from the SSISDB catalog.

questions.q: Running a package inside SSDT by pressing the start/debug button is best described as:
options: A design-time test run, not a production execution against the SSISDB catalog
Exactly identical to a scheduled SQL Server Agent execution from the catalog
An operation that automatically deploys the project to SSISDB
Something that requires the legacy Integration Services service to be running
questions.explain: Running a package from inside SSDT is a design-time test run on your own machine — it is not the same as a production execution of a deployed project from the SSISDB catalog.
